newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-SAO PAULO PLAYERS IGNORE PARREIRA'S WARNING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SAO PAULO PLAYERS IGNORE PARREIRA'S WARNING.

text.p: Sao Paulo, given a stern lecture by coach Carlos Alberto Parreira about their poor disciplinary record last week, had eight players booked and one sent off in the Brazilian championship at the weekend.
Parreira read the riot act after former international striker Muller became the team's seventh player to be sent off in four games against Atletico Paranaense in midweek.
But his words seemed to have little affect as the cards once again flowed. Midfielder Denilson was dismissed 10 minutes from the end for retaliation.
Parreira's problems increased as Atletico Mineiro came from behind to win 2-1 with an 88th-minute penalty converted by striker Euler, a former Sao Paulo player.
Sao Paulo, who threw away a two-goal lead as they were held 3-3 by Atletico Paranaense, have won only once in their last nine games and have slipped from first to 14th in the table.
The top eight teams qualify for the quarter-finals.
Palmeiras lost for the first time in the tournament while Flamengo, the country's best-supported club, were beaten 4-1 for the third time in four games.

Palmeiras's 2-0 defeat against Atletico Paranaense was only their third this year and cost them the leadership. Atletico's goals came in the first quarter of an hour through strikers Oseas and Paulo Rink.

Flamengo's defeat at home to lowly Parana was their fourth straight loss. Brazilian international Bebeto had a miserable day despite scoring the team's consolation goal. He missed one gilt-edged chance from six metres and hit the post twice.
